title: Florence and the Medici

match.reason: The closest bank point, Patrons and the Medici, covers patronage in general and the Medici as wealthy art patrons, but it does not teach that the Medici ruled Florence or that Florence was a centre of Renaissance art, so the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Florence and the Medici
card: Florence was a rich city in Italy. Its wealth came from trade and banking, and it was a city-state, a city that governed itself and its nearby land.
The Medici were a banking family. Over many years they became the most powerful family in Florence and ruled the city, often without holding a title such as king.
The Medici used their wealth to pay artists and scholars. Paying for art and learning in this way is called patronage.
Patronage drew talented people to Florence. Their work made the city a centre of Renaissance art.
draft.remember: The Medici used banking wealth to pay artists and scholars, and Florence became a centre of Renaissance art.

a.q: How did the Medici family help make Florence a centre of Renaissance art?
opts: They paid artists and scholars to work there
They painted most of the city's great artworks
They banned artists from working in other cities
They taught art to every child in Florence
a.why: The Medici had wealth from banking and used it to pay artists and scholars. This is patronage. The family did not paint the works themselves, they paid the people who made them.
a.clue: Think about what banking wealth could be spent on.

b.q: A wealthy banker in Florence pays a sculptor to carve a statue for the city and also pays a scholar to study old books. What is this an example of?
b.why: Paying artists and scholars to do their work is patronage, as the Medici did. Trade is buying and selling goods, which is a different idea, even though trade helped make Florence rich.
b.clue: Which word means paying for art and learning?

a.best: They paid artists and scholars to work there
